description: Database initialization creates the domains table with all columns (id TEXT PK, name TEXT NOT NULL, color TEXT NOT NULL, icon TEXT, sort_order REAL, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)
steps: Step 1: Start the backend server
Step 2: Send GET /api/health or equivalent to confirm server is running
Step 3: Query the database schema for the domains table

Step 4: Verify columns: id (TEXT PK), name (TEXT NOT NULL), color (TEXT NOT NULL), icon (TEXT), sort_order (REAL DEFAULT 0.0), created_at (TEXT NOT NULL), updated_at (TEXT NOT NULL), deleted_at (TEXT)
Step 5: Verify the partial index idx_domains_sort exists on sort_order WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

description: Database initialization creates the projects table with FK to domains and all columns including status CHECK constraint
steps: Step 1: Query the database schema for the projects table

Step 2: Verify columns: id, domain_id (FK to domains), name, description, status (CHECK: active/someday/completed/archived), default_view (CHECK: list/kanban/timeline/materials), last_touched_at, last_context_note, deadline, sort_order, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 3: Verify index idx_projects_domain on (domain_id, sort_order) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
Step 4: Verify index idx_projects_status on (status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
Step 5: Verify index idx_projects_last_touched on (last_touched_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active'

description: Database initialization creates the tasks table with all columns, FK to projects, recurrence fields, and CHECK constraints
steps: Step 1: Query the database schema for the tasks table

Step 2: Verify columns: id, project_id (FK), title, status (CHECK: backlog/active/done/dropped), kanban_column, estimated_minutes, due_date, seasonal_window, depends_on (DEFAULT '[]'), sort_order, notes, completed_at, recurrence_rule, recurrence_parent_id (FK to tasks), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 3: Verify index idx_tasks_project on (project_id, sort_order) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
Step 4: Verify index idx_tasks_status on (status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
Step 5: Verify index idx_tasks_due_date on (due_date) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND due_date IS NOT NULL
Step 6: Verify index idx_tasks_completed on (completed_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND completed_at IS NOT NULL

description: Database initialization creates inbox_items, daily_plans, and time_blocks tables with correct schemas
steps: Step 1: Query schema for inbox_items table — verify columns: id, type (CHECK: text/voice/photo), raw_text, audio_path, photo_path, ocr_text, quick_note, processed_at, processed_to_task_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 2: Verify index idx_inbox_unprocessed on (created_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND processed_at IS NULL

Step 3: Query schema for daily_plans table — verify columns: id, date (UNIQUE), available_minutes, buffer_percent, reflection_note, morning_ritual_completed_at, close_out_completed_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 4: Verify unique index idx_daily_plans_date on (date) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Step 5: Query schema for time_blocks table — verify columns: id, daily_plan_id (FK), domain_id (FK), start_time, end_time, theme, task_ids (DEFAULT '[]'), sort_order, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 6: Verify index idx_time_blocks_plan on (daily_plan_id, start_time) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

description: Database initialization creates task_events, tags, task_tags, and remaining tables (materials, attachments, seasonal_config, calendar_events, weekly_theme_templates, weekly_theme_blocks)
steps: Step 1: Query schema for task_events table — verify columns: id, task_id (FK), event_type (CHECK constraint), old_value, new_value, occurred_at, daily_plan_id (FK), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 2: Query schema for tags table — verify: id, name (UNIQUE), color, sort_order, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
Step 3: Query schema for task_tags junction table — verify: id, task_id (FK), tag_id (FK), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at with unique index on (task_id, tag_id)
Step 4: Query schema for materials table — verify all columns including blocks_tasks (DEFAULT '[]')
Step 5: Query schema for attachments table — verify polymorphic FKs (task_id, project_id, inbox_item_id, material_id)
Step 6: Query schema for seasonal_config — verify key (UNIQUE), value, year, notes
Step 7: Query schema for calendar_events — verify all columns including source CHECK and external_id
Step 8: Query schema for weekly_theme_templates and weekly_theme_blocks — verify template_id FK, day_of_week CHECK (1-7)

description: Create a domain via POST /api/domains with ULID primary key, name, color, and icon
steps: Step 1: Send POST /api/domains with body {name: 'W-2 Job', color: '#3B82F6', icon: 'briefcase'}
Step 2: Verify response status 201 and response contains id (ULID format), name, color, icon
Step 3: Verify id is a valid ULID (26 alphanumeric characters, time-sortable)
Step 4: Verify created_at and updated_at are set to ISO 8601 timestamps
Step 5: Send GET /api/domains and verify the new domain appears in the list

description: Read all active domains via GET /api/domains, sorted by sort_order, excluding soft-deleted rows
steps: Step 1: Create three domains with different sort_order values (1.0, 2.0, 3.0)
Step 2: Soft-delete the second domain (sort_order 2.0)
Step 3: Send GET /api/domains
Step 4: Verify only two domains returned, sorted by sort_order ascending
Step 5: Verify the soft-deleted domain is not in the results

description: Update a domain's name, color, and icon via PATCH /api/domains/:id
steps: Step 1: Create a domain with name 'Test Domain'
Step 2: Send PATCH /api/domains/:id with {name: 'Updated Domain', color: '#10B981'}
Step 3: Verify response shows updated values
Step 4: Verify updated_at timestamp changed from created_at
Step 5: Send GET /api/domains/:id and confirm changes persisted

description: Soft-delete a domain via DELETE /api/domains/:id sets deleted_at instead of removing the row
steps: Step 1: Create a domain
Step 2: Send DELETE /api/domains/:id
Step 3: Verify response indicates success
Step 4: Send GET /api/domains — verify domain does not appear in active list
Step 5: Query database directly to confirm row exists with non-null deleted_at

description: Create a project via POST /api/projects with domain_id FK, name, status defaults, and default_view
steps: Step 1: Create a domain first
Step 2: Send POST /api/projects with {domain_id, name: 'Greenhouse Build', description: 'Main greenhouse project'}
Step 3: Verify response has ULID id, status defaults to 'active', default_view defaults to 'list'
Step 4: Verify domain_id FK is set correctly
Step 5: Send GET /api/projects?domain_id=:id and verify project appears

description: Create a task via POST /api/tasks with project_id FK, title, and verify defaults
steps: Step 1: Create a domain and project
Step 2: Send POST /api/tasks with {project_id, title: 'Pour foundation footings'}
Step 3: Verify response has ULID id, status defaults to 'backlog', sort_order is set
Step 4: Verify depends_on defaults to '[]' (empty JSON array)
Step 5: Verify completed_at is NULL
Step 6: Send GET /api/tasks?project_id=:id and verify task appears

description: Completing a task sets status to 'done' and populates completed_at with ISO 8601 timestamp
steps: Step 1: Create a domain, project, and task
Step 2: Send PATCH /api/tasks/:id with {status: 'done'}
Step 3: Verify response shows status = 'done'
Step 4: Verify completed_at is set to a valid ISO 8601 timestamp
Step 5: Verify a task_event was logged with event_type = 'completed'

description: Create an inbox item via POST /api/inbox with type='text' and raw_text
steps: Step 1: Send POST /api/inbox with {type: 'text', raw_text: 'Check greenhouse lumber order'}
Step 2: Verify response has ULID id, type = 'text', processed_at = null
Step 3: Send GET /api/inbox?unprocessed=true and verify the item appears
Step 4: Verify the item's created_at is a valid ISO 8601 timestamp

description: Task event is logged when a task is created, including event_type='created'
steps: Step 1: Create a domain and project
Step 2: Create a task in the project
Step 3: Send GET /api/task-events?task_id=:id
Step 4: Verify at least one event with event_type = 'created' and occurred_at timestamp

description: Soft-delete cascade: deleting a project also soft-deletes its child tasks and materials
steps: Step 1: Create a domain, project, two tasks, and one material in the project
Step 2: Send DELETE /api/projects/:id to soft-delete the project
Step 3: Verify the project has deleted_at set
Step 4: Send GET /api/tasks?project_id=:id — verify no active tasks returned
Step 5: Query database to confirm child tasks have deleted_at set
Step 6: Query database to confirm child materials have deleted_at set

description: Create a daily plan via POST /api/daily-plans with date, available_minutes, and buffer_percent
steps: Step 1: Send POST /api/daily-plans with {date: '2026-02-22', available_minutes: 480, buffer_percent: 20}
Step 2: Verify response has ULID id, date is set, morning_ritual_completed_at is NULL
Step 3: Send GET /api/daily-plans?date=2026-02-22 and verify the plan exists
Step 4: Verify the UNIQUE constraint prevents creating a second plan for the same date

description: Domains reorder via fractional indexing — PATCH sort_order with REAL values allows inserting between existing items
steps: Step 1: Create three domains with sort_order 1.0, 2.0, 3.0
Step 2: Move the third domain between the first and second by setting sort_order to 1.5
Step 3: Send GET /api/domains
Step 4: Verify order is: domain1 (1.0), domain3 (1.5), domain2 (2.0)

description: Task status CHECK constraint prevents invalid status values
steps: Step 1: Create a domain, project, and task
Step 2: Attempt to PATCH task with {status: 'invalid_status'}
Step 3: Verify the server returns an error (400 or 422)
Step 4: Verify the task status remains unchanged

description: Text capture via inline text field on Inbox screen — type text, press Enter, item appears in queue
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Inbox screen in the browser
Step 2: Locate the quick capture text field ('What's on your mind?')
Step 3: Click into the field and type 'Check greenhouse lumber order -- need 10ft not 8ft'
Step 4: Press Enter
Step 5: Verify the text field is cleared
Step 6: Verify a new item appears in the Unprocessed queue below
Step 7: Verify the item shows the captured text and a timestamp

description: Global keyboard shortcut (Cmd+Shift+I) opens a lightweight capture overlay from any screen
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 2: Press Cmd+Shift+I (or the configured shortcut)
Step 3: Verify a capture overlay appears (not a full page navigation)
Step 4: Verify the overlay contains a single text field with placeholder text
Step 5: Verify the rest of the screen is dimmed but visible behind the overlay

description: Capture overlay: typing text and pressing Enter saves to inbox, shows confirmation, and dismisses overlay
steps: Step 1: Open the capture overlay via Cmd+Shift+I from any screen
Step 2: Type 'Buy dog food -- running low'
Step 3: Press Enter
Step 4: Verify a brief confirmation appears ('Captured' or similar)
Step 5: Verify the overlay dismisses and returns to the previous screen
Step 6: Navigate to the Inbox screen
Step 7: Verify the new item 'Buy dog food -- running low' appears in the unprocessed queue

description: Capture overlay: pressing Escape closes the overlay without saving any item
steps: Step 1: Note the current inbox unprocessed count
Step 2: Open the capture overlay via Cmd+Shift+I
Step 3: Type some text in the field
Step 4: Press Escape
Step 5: Verify the overlay closes
Step 6: Navigate to Inbox and verify the count has not changed — no item was created

description: Inbox screen displays unprocessed items in FIFO order (oldest first) with type icon, text preview, and timestamp
steps: Step 1: Create three inbox items via the API with different timestamps
Step 2: Navigate to the Inbox screen
Step 3: Verify all three items appear in the Unprocessed section
Step 4: Verify items are ordered oldest first (FIFO — first captured, first shown)
Step 5: Verify each item shows a type icon (Aa for text), text preview, and timestamp

description: Inbox badge count on sidebar shows number of unprocessed items and updates in real-time
steps: Step 1: Navigate to any screen and observe the Inbox badge count in the sidebar
Step 2: Note the current count (e.g., 0)
Step 3: Use the capture overlay (Cmd+Shift+I) to create a new inbox item
Step 4: Verify the badge count increments by 1
Step 5: Navigate to Inbox and process one item
Step 6: Verify the badge count decrements by 1

description: Card-by-card processing flow: clicking 'Process All' presents unprocessed items one at a time with 5 GTD-style action buttons
steps: Step 1: Create 3 unprocessed inbox items via the API
Step 2: Navigate to the Inbox screen
Step 3: Click 'Process All' button
Step 4: Verify a processing modal/view opens showing the first (oldest) item
Step 5: Verify 5 action buttons are visible: Create Task, Someday/Maybe, Reference, Do It Now, Delete
Step 6: Click 'Create Task' — verify domain/project picker appears
Step 7: Select a domain and project, set estimate to 30 minutes, click confirm
Step 8: Verify the item is marked as processed and the next item is presented
Step 9: Click 'Delete' on the second item — verify it's soft-deleted and next item appears
Step 10: Click 'Reference' on the third item — verify it's marked as processed
Step 11: Verify processing flow completes and returns to the Inbox screen
Step 12: Verify the unprocessed count is now 0

description: Processing: 'Create Task' action creates a task in selected project and links inbox item via processed_to_task_id
steps: Step 1: Create a domain and project via the API
Step 2: Create an inbox item with raw_text 'Write API tests'
Step 3: Navigate to Inbox and start processing
Step 4: Select 'Create Task' action
Step 5: Choose the domain and project from the picker
Step 6: Set estimated_minutes to 60
Step 7: Confirm task creation
Step 8: Verify inbox item now has processed_at set and processed_to_task_id pointing to the new task
Step 9: Navigate to the project and verify the new task exists with the correct title and estimate

description: Processing: 'Delete' action soft-deletes the inbox item
steps: Step 1: Create an inbox item via the API
Step 2: Navigate to Inbox and click on the item to process it
Step 3: Click the 'Delete' action
Step 4: Verify the item disappears from the unprocessed queue
Step 5: Verify the inbox badge count decrements

description: Processing: 'Do It Now' action starts a 2-minute timer for quick tasks
steps: Step 1: Create an inbox item with raw_text 'Reply to quick email'
Step 2: Navigate to Inbox and start processing the item
Step 3: Click 'Do It Now' action
Step 4: Verify a 2-minute countdown timer appears
Step 5: Verify the item is marked as processed after the timer completes or user dismisses

description: Domain CRUD via Settings or API: create a domain with name, color, icon and see it in the sidebar and Projects screen domain tabs
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Domains (or use the API)
Step 2: Create a new domain named 'Homestead' with color '#F59E0B' and icon 'tractor'
Step 3: Verify the domain appears in the sidebar domain list with the correct color
Step 4: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 5: Verify a domain tab for 'Homestead' appears with the orange color

description: Domain: reorder domains via drag-and-drop in Settings, reflecting in sidebar navigation
steps: Step 1: Create three domains: 'W-2 Job', 'Freelance', 'Homestead'
Step 2: Navigate to Settings > Domains
Step 3: Drag 'Homestead' above 'Freelance'
Step 4: Verify the sort order updates (fractional indexing)
Step 5: Navigate to a different screen and verify the sidebar domain list reflects the new order

description: Domain: at least one domain must exist — prevent deleting the last domain
steps: Step 1: Ensure only one domain exists
Step 2: Attempt to delete or archive the last domain
Step 3: Verify the system prevents deletion with an appropriate error message
Step 4: Verify the domain still exists

description: Project CRUD: create a project within a domain with name, description, default_view, and optional deadline
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 2: Select a domain tab
Step 3: Click 'New Project'
Step 4: Enter name 'Greenhouse Build', description 'Main greenhouse construction project', leave default_view as 'list'
Step 5: Set a deadline date
Step 6: Click create/save
Step 7: Verify the project card appears under the selected domain
Step 8: Verify the project card shows the name, task count (0), and deadline

description: Project list view shows tasks sorted by sort_order, grouped by status (Active/Backlog/Done)
steps: Step 1: Create a project with several tasks in different statuses (2 backlog, 1 active, 1 done)
Step 2: Navigate to the project in list view
Step 3: Verify tasks are grouped by status sections
Step 4: Verify within each group, tasks are sorted by sort_order
Step 5: Verify completed tasks appear at the bottom with strikethrough styling

description: Rapid sequential task entry: type title, press Enter, task is created immediately and focus moves to new empty input
steps: Step 1: Navigate to a project's list view
Step 2: Click the task input field at the top
Step 3: Type 'Pour foundation footings' and press Enter
Step 4: Verify the task appears in the list immediately
Step 5: Verify the input field is cleared and focused for the next entry
Step 6: Type 'Frame south wall' and press Enter
Step 7: Verify the second task appears below the first
Step 8: Type 'Frame north wall' and press Enter
Step 9: Type 'Install ridge beam' and press Enter
Step 10: Verify all four tasks exist in the list in creation order
Step 11: Verify each task has status = 'backlog' and sequential sort_order values

description: Drag-to-reorder tasks in list view updates sort_order via fractional indexing
steps: Step 1: Create a project with 4 tasks in order: A, B, C, D
Step 2: Navigate to the project list view
Step 3: Drag task D between tasks A and B
Step 4: Verify the visual order is now A, D, B, C
Step 5: Refresh the page and verify the order persists

description: Task: mark as done via checkbox click — sets status to 'done' and completed_at timestamp
steps: Step 1: Navigate to a project with tasks in list view
Step 2: Click the checkbox next to an active task
Step 3: Verify the task visually shows as completed (strikethrough, moves to Done section)
Step 4: Verify via API that task status is 'done' and completed_at is set

description: Task: set and clear due date, set estimated_minutes via task detail or inline editing
steps: Step 1: Navigate to a project and click on a task to open its detail view
Step 2: Set a due date to '2026-03-15'
Step 3: Set estimated_minutes to 90
Step 4: Save and verify both fields are persisted
Step 5: Clear the due date (set to null)
Step 6: Verify due_date is now null while estimated_minutes remains 90

description: Project cards on Projects screen show name, task counts, default view, deadline, and last-touched date with stale warnings (7+ days)
steps: Step 1: Create a domain with two projects
Step 2: Add 5 tasks to project 1 (3 backlog, 2 done)
Step 3: Set project 2's last_touched_at to 10 days ago via API
Step 4: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 5: Verify project 1 card shows: name, '3 active / 2 done', default view icon
Step 6: Verify project 2 card shows a stale warning indicator (7+ days)

description: Domain tabs on Projects screen filter projects by domain, with an ALL tab showing projects grouped by domain
steps: Step 1: Create two domains ('W-2 Job', 'Homestead') with 2 projects each
Step 2: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 3: Verify an 'ALL' tab and individual domain tabs are visible
Step 4: Click the 'W-2 Job' tab — verify only W-2 Job projects are shown
Step 5: Click the 'Homestead' tab — verify only Homestead projects are shown
Step 6: Click 'ALL' — verify all projects shown, grouped by domain

description: Project: update status to someday, completed, or archived
steps: Step 1: Create a project with status 'active'
Step 2: Update status to 'someday' and verify via API
Step 3: Update status to 'active' and verify
Step 4: Update status to 'completed' and verify
Step 5: Update status to 'archived' and verify

description: Creating a task in a project updates the project's last_touched_at timestamp
steps: Step 1: Create a domain and project, note the project's last_touched_at
Step 2: Wait 1 second, then create a task in the project
Step 3: Fetch the project and verify last_touched_at has been updated to a more recent timestamp

description: Cockpit creates or retrieves today's daily plan when navigated to
steps: Step 1: Ensure no daily plan exists for today
Step 2: Navigate to the Cockpit screen
Step 3: Verify the Cockpit loads and either creates a new daily plan or prompts the morning ritual
Step 4: Verify a daily_plans row exists for today's date

description: Morning ritual: 5-stage progress bar renders and stages navigate forward and back
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Cockpit with no ritual completed for today
Step 2: Verify the morning ritual flow appears with a progress bar showing 5 stages
Step 3: Verify Stage 1 (Review Yesterday) is displayed
Step 4: Complete Stage 1 and tap Next
Step 5: Verify Stage 2 is displayed and the progress bar advances
Step 6: Tap Back and verify Stage 1 is displayed again
Step 7: Navigate forward through remaining stages

description: Morning ritual Stage 1: Review Yesterday — shows completed and uncompleted tasks from yesterday with forced options
steps: Step 1: Create a daily plan for yesterday with 2 time blocks containing 5 tasks total
Step 2: Mark 3 tasks as done and leave 2 incomplete
Step 3: Navigate to the Cockpit for today and start the morning ritual
Step 4: Verify Stage 1 is displayed with title 'Review Yesterday'
Step 5: Verify a 'Completed' column shows 3 tasks with green checkmarks and domain color badges
Step 6: Verify a 'Not Completed' column shows 2 tasks with amber indicators
Step 7: For the first uncompleted task, verify three options: 'Reschedule to today', 'Push to later this week', 'Return to project backlog'
Step 8: Select 'Reschedule to today' for the first task
Step 9: Verify a task_event is logged with event_type = 'rescheduled'
Step 10: Select 'Return to project backlog' for the second task
Step 11: Verify a task_event is logged for the second decision
Step 12: Tap 'Next' and verify progression to Stage 2

description: Morning ritual Stage 2: Check What's Due — shows tasks due today, overdue tasks, calendar events, and seasonal alerts
steps: Step 1: Create 2 tasks with due_date = today in different domains
Step 2: Create 1 task with due_date = 3 days ago (overdue) in a third domain
Step 3: Create a calendar event for today (Team standup 9:00-9:30)
Step 4: Navigate to Cockpit, start ritual, advance to Stage 2
Step 5: Verify the due-today tasks are listed with their domain color badges
Step 6: Verify the overdue task is listed with an overdue indicator
Step 7: Verify the calendar event is shown with time details
Step 8: Acknowledge a due-today task to add it to today's plan
Step 9: Verify the overdue task can be rescheduled or returned to backlog
Step 10: Tap 'Next' and verify progression to Stage 3

description: Morning ritual: completing all stages sets daily_plans.morning_ritual_completed_at
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Cockpit and complete all 5 morning ritual stages
Step 2: After tapping 'Finish Ritual', verify the Cockpit shows the day view (not the ritual flow)
Step 3: Query the API for today's daily plan
Step 4: Verify morning_ritual_completed_at is set to a valid ISO 8601 timestamp

description: Cockpit day view: after ritual completion, shows vertical timeline of time blocks with assigned tasks and capacity bar
steps: Step 1: Complete the morning ritual with time blocks and assigned tasks
Step 2: Verify the Cockpit day view shows a vertical timeline
Step 3: Verify each time block shows start/end time, domain color, and assigned tasks
Step 4: Verify the capacity bar is visible showing committed vs. available minutes

description: First-time setup wizard launches automatically when no database/domains exist
steps: Step 1: Start the app with a fresh/empty database
Step 2: Navigate to the app in the browser
Step 3: Verify the setup wizard launches automatically (not the main app screens)
Step 4: Verify the wizard shows a welcome message and 'Let's set up your system' button

description: Setup wizard Step 1: Create domains with name, color picker, icon selector, drag-to-reorder. Pre-filled suggestions available
steps: Step 1: Start the setup wizard and reach the Domains screen
Step 2: Verify pre-filled domain suggestions are displayed (e.g., W-2 Job, Freelance, Apps, Homestead, Personal)
Step 3: Edit a domain name (e.g., change 'Apps' to 'Side Projects')
Step 4: Change a domain's color using the color picker and verify the preview updates
Step 5: Select an icon for a domain from the icon selector
Step 6: Click 'Add Domain' to add a new domain named 'Learning' with yellow color
Step 7: Verify the new domain appears in the list
Step 8: Delete one of the suggested domains by clicking its remove button
Step 9: Drag to reorder domains — place W-2 Job first and Personal last
Step 10: Verify the visual order matches the drag result
Step 11: Tap 'Continue' and verify navigation to Step 2

description: Setup wizard Step 2: Configure work hours per day with start/end time pickers and buffer slider
steps: Step 1: Arrive at Step 2 of the setup wizard
Step 2: Verify a weekly grid is displayed with each day of the week
Step 3: Set Monday hours to 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM using the time pickers
Step 4: Set Tuesday through Friday to the same hours
Step 5: Set Saturday to 8:00 AM - 1:00 PM
Step 6: Toggle Sunday to 'OFF' and verify the time pickers are disabled for Sunday
Step 7: Verify the buffer slider defaults to 20%
Step 8: Adjust buffer to 25% and verify the weekly total updates
Step 9: Verify effective capacity is displayed (total hours minus buffer)
Step 10: Tap 'Continue' and verify navigation to Step 3

description: Setup wizard Step 3: Seasonal configuration is optional — toggle on to enter USDA zone and frost dates
steps: Step 1: Arrive at Step 3 of the setup wizard
Step 2: Verify a toggle asks 'Do you manage seasonal or outdoor projects?'
Step 3: Toggle to 'Yes'
Step 4: Enter USDA planting zone '7b'
Step 5: Enter last frost date 'April 15'
Step 6: Enter first frost date 'October 20'
Step 7: Tap 'Continue' to proceed to Summary

description: Setup wizard: Summary confirmation screen shows all entered data and completing setup drops user into Cockpit
steps: Step 1: Complete all 3 setup wizard steps with domains, work hours, and seasonal config
Step 2: Verify the Summary screen displays the domain count with color swatches
Step 3: Verify the weekly schedule summary shows hours per day
Step 4: Verify the buffer percentage is displayed
Step 5: Verify seasonal data (zone, frost dates) is shown
Step 6: Tap 'Start Using GroundWork'
Step 7: Verify all domains exist in the database via API
Step 8: Verify seasonal_config rows exist for last-frost-date, first-frost-date, planting-zone
Step 9: Verify a daily_plans row exists for today with correct available_minutes
Step 10: Verify a default weekly_theme_template was created
Step 11: Verify the user lands on the Cockpit screen with an empty-state welcome message

description: Setup wizard: toggling seasonal config OFF skips seasonal fields entirely and creates no seasonal_config rows
steps: Step 1: Start the setup wizard and complete Steps 1-2
Step 2: On Step 3, leave the seasonal toggle as 'No' (or toggle it OFF)
Step 3: Tap Continue to the Summary screen
Step 4: Complete the wizard
Step 5: Query the API and verify no seasonal_config rows were created

description: Settings: Domain management — create, rename, recolor, re-icon, and archive domains with color picker
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Domains
Step 2: Verify the existing domains are listed with their colors and icons
Step 3: Click 'Add Domain' to create a new domain named 'Learning' with color '#8B5CF6'
Step 4: Verify the new domain appears in the list with the correct color
Step 5: Click on the 'Learning' domain to edit it
Step 6: Change its name to 'Education'
Step 7: Change its color to '#06B6D4'
Step 8: Change its icon
Step 9: Save and verify changes are reflected in the sidebar domain list
Step 10: Navigate to the Projects screen and verify the domain tab shows the updated name and color

description: Settings: Work hours configuration — per-day start/end time pickers with OFF toggle and buffer slider (0-50%)
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Work Hours
Step 2: Verify per-day time pickers are displayed for each day of the week
Step 3: Verify current values match what was set during onboarding
Step 4: Change Monday's hours from 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM to 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
Step 5: Toggle Saturday to OFF
Step 6: Adjust buffer slider from 20% to 30%
Step 7: Verify the weekly total hours updates to reflect the changes
Step 8: Verify the effective capacity display updates (total - buffer%)
Step 9: Save settings and refresh the page
Step 10: Verify all changes persist after refresh

description: Sidebar navigation renders with GroundWork branding, 5 screen icons (Inbox, Cockpit, Projects, Review, Settings), domain list with colors, and sync status
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the app in the browser
Step 2: Verify the left sidebar is visible with GroundWork branding at the top
Step 3: Verify 5 navigation items are present: Inbox, Cockpit, Projects, Review, Settings
Step 4: Verify the domain list section shows all domains with their assigned colors
Step 5: Verify a sync status indicator (dot) is visible at the bottom of the sidebar
Step 6: Click each navigation item and verify the main content area changes

description: Active navigation state highlights the current screen in the sidebar; domain color squares use the correct hex values from the domains table

Step 4: Verify the processing card shows the photo and OCR text
Step 5: Click 'Link to Materials'
Step 6: Verify the system searches materials and shows 'Polycarbonate panels' as a match
Step 7: Link the item to the material and verify the material's unit_cost is updated

description: Processing flow for voice items: edit transcription before creating task
steps: Step 1: Create a voice inbox item with imperfect transcription
Step 2: Process the item
Step 3: Edit the transcription text to correct errors
Step 4: Create a task from the corrected text
Step 5: Verify the task title uses the corrected text

description: Seasonal configuration: enter USDA planting zone, last frost date, and first frost date in Settings
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Seasonal Config
Step 2: Enter planting zone '7b'
Step 3: Enter last frost date 'April 15'
Step 4: Enter first frost date 'October 20'
Step 5: Save and verify seasonal_config rows are created for each key

description: Seasonal configuration: year-specific overrides — add an override for a specific year that takes precedence
steps: Step 1: Set default last frost date to April 15
Step 2: Add a year-specific override: last frost date for 2026 = May 1
Step 3: Verify the override row exists with year = 2026
Step 4: Verify queries for 2026's last frost date return May 1
Step 5: Verify queries for 2027 still return the default April 15

description: Weekly review: pre-computed digest shows completed tasks per domain (bar chart), overdue count, stalled project count, inbox backlog, upcoming deadlines
steps: Step 1: Create completed tasks across 3 domains over the past week
Step 2: Create overdue tasks (due_date < today)
Step 3: Create stalled projects (last_touched_at > 7 days ago)
Step 4: Leave some inbox items unprocessed
Step 5: Create tasks with due_date within next 14 days
Step 6: Navigate to the Review screen
Step 7: Verify the digest overview shows: completed task counts per domain, overdue count, stalled project count, inbox backlog count, upcoming deadlines list

description: Weekly review: overdue triage with forced decisions — each overdue task must be addressed before proceeding
steps: Step 1: Create 4 overdue tasks across 2 domains
Step 2: Navigate to the Review screen and start the overdue triage section
Step 3: Verify all 4 overdue tasks are listed with domain color badges
Step 4: For each task, verify 4 options: reschedule (date picker), remove due date, drop, mark done
Step 5: Reschedule task 1 to next Monday
Step 6: Remove due date from task 2
Step 7: Drop task 3
Step 8: Mark task 4 as done
Step 9: Verify the user cannot proceed to the next section until all tasks are addressed
Step 10: Verify task_events are logged for each decision

description: Weekly review: overdue tasks grouped by domain when 5+ overdue items exist
steps: Step 1: Create 6 overdue tasks across 3 domains (2 per domain)
Step 2: Navigate to the Review overdue triage section
Step 3: Verify tasks are grouped by domain with domain color headers
Step 4: Verify each group shows its domain name and task count

description: Weekly review: stalled project decisions — Acknowledge, Pause (someday), Archive, Add context note, Create follow-up task
steps: Step 1: Create 3 active projects with last_touched_at older than 7 days
Step 2: Navigate to the Review stalled projects section
Step 3: Verify all 3 projects are listed with last_touched_at dates
Step 4: Select 'Acknowledge' for project 1 — verify it's dismissed
Step 5: Select 'Pause' for project 2 — verify status changes to 'someday'
Step 6: Select 'Add context note' for project 3 — enter a note
Step 7: Verify the context note is saved to the project's last_context_note
Step 8: Verify the user can also 'Create follow-up task' for a stalled project

description: Weekly review: horizon check — domain balance pie chart from time_blocks duration grouped by domain_id for past 7 days
steps: Step 1: Create time blocks over the past 7 days distributed across domains
Step 2: Navigate to the Review horizon check section
Step 3: Verify a domain balance visualization (pie/donut chart) is displayed
Step 4: Verify each domain's percentage matches the time_blocks data
Step 5: Verify a reflection text area is available for free-form notes

description: Weekly review: someday/maybe scan — lists all projects with status='someday' with actions: Keep, Promote to Active, Archive
steps: Step 1: Create 3 projects with status = 'someday'
Step 2: Navigate to the Review someday/maybe section
Step 3: Verify all 3 someday projects are listed with name, domain, creation date, task count
Step 4: Select 'Keep' for project 1 — verify it stays as someday
Step 5: Select 'Promote to Active' for project 2 — verify status changes to 'active'
Step 6: Select 'Archive' for project 3 — verify status changes to 'archived'

description: Weekly review: completion timestamp recorded and displayed on Review screen
steps: Step 1: Complete all sections of the weekly review
Step 2: Verify a completion timestamp is recorded
Step 3: Navigate away and return to the Review screen
Step 4: Verify the screen shows 'Last reviewed: [date]'

description: Weekly review: next week theme adjustments — view/edit template blocks for the coming week without modifying the base template
steps: Step 1: Set up an active weekly theme template
Step 2: Navigate to the Review and find the theme adjustment section
Step 3: View the upcoming week's blocks from the template
Step 4: Make an adjustment (e.g., swap a block's domain for one day)
Step 5: Verify the adjustment creates a day-specific override
Step 6: Verify the base template remains unchanged

description: Full weekly review end-to-end workflow: digest → overdue triage → stalled projects → horizon check → someday/maybe → theme adjustments → completion
steps: Step 1: Set up data: completed tasks, overdue tasks, stalled projects, someday projects, time blocks
Step 2: Navigate to the Review screen
Step 3: View the digest overview with all metrics
Step 4: Enter overdue triage — make forced decisions on all overdue tasks
Step 5: Enter stalled projects — acknowledge or take action on each
Step 6: Enter horizon check — view domain balance chart and write reflection
Step 7: Enter someday/maybe scan — decide on each someday project
Step 8: View/adjust next week's theme blocks
Step 9: Complete the review
Step 10: Verify completion timestamp is set
Step 11: Verify all decisions resulted in appropriate database updates and task_events

description: Weekly review: overdue triage cannot be skipped — user must address every overdue task before proceeding
steps: Step 1: Create 3 overdue tasks
Step 2: Navigate to the overdue triage section
Step 3: Address only 2 of 3 tasks
Step 4: Attempt to proceed to the next section
Step 5: Verify the system prevents proceeding until all tasks are addressed

description: FTS5 virtual tables exist for tasks, projects, inbox_items, and materials with correct content columns
steps: Step 1: Query database to verify tasks_fts exists with columns: title, notes, kanban_column
Step 2: Verify projects_fts exists with columns: name, description, last_context_note
Step 3: Verify inbox_items_fts exists with columns: raw_text, ocr_text, quick_note
Step 4: Verify materials_fts exists with columns: name, source, notes

description: Task events are logged for all major task mutations: created, status_changed, completed, rescheduled, estimate_changed
steps: Step 1: Create a task — verify 'created' event logged
Step 2: Change task status — verify 'status_changed' event with old_value and new_value
Step 3: Mark task as done — verify 'completed' event
Step 4: Reschedule the task via cockpit — verify 'rescheduled' event
Step 5: Change estimated_minutes — verify 'estimate_changed' event

description: Sync status indicator shows green dot when peer found via mDNS, gray dot when no peers
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the app with no other devices on the network
Step 2: Verify the sync indicator in the sidebar shows a gray dot with 'No peers' text
Step 3: Verify the sync indicator is visible and not clipped or hidden

description: Settings: Sync and Devices section shows connected peers, last sync timestamp, and device management
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Sync & Devices
Step 2: Verify the section shows a 'Connected Peers' area (empty if no peers)
Step 3: Verify a 'Last sync' timestamp is displayed
Step 4: Verify device management options are visible (even if no paired devices)

description: Weekly review: stalled project 'Archive' action changes project status to archived and removes it from active project lists
steps: Step 1: Create an active project with last_touched_at older than 7 days
Step 2: Navigate to the Review stalled projects section
Step 3: Select 'Archive' for the stalled project
Step 4: Verify the project's status changes to 'archived'
Step 5: Navigate to the Projects screen and verify the project no longer appears in the active list

description: Catch-Up Mode activates when user opens app after 1-6 days of absence — calm tone, skippable inbox, compact overdue triage
steps: Step 1: Set up data simulating 3 days of absence: no daily_plans for past 3 days
Step 2: Create 8 overdue tasks across 3 domains
Step 3: Create 5 unprocessed inbox items
Step 4: Navigate to the Cockpit
Step 5: Verify the app detects the absence and activates Catch-Up Mode
Step 6: Verify the tone is calm and non-judgmental — no guilt language like 'You missed 3 days'
Step 7: Verify inbox processing step is present but has a 'Skip' option
Step 8: Verify overdue triage is compact with one-tap actions grouped by domain
Step 9: Process overdue tasks using quick actions (reschedule, backlog, drop)
Step 10: Verify a stalled project scan is presented after overdue triage
Step 11: Complete the catch-up flow and verify the system transitions to Build Your Day

description: Catch-Up Mode: compact overdue triage with one-tap domain-grouped actions, completable in under 10 minutes
steps: Step 1: Create 15 overdue tasks across 4 domains
Step 2: Simulate 3-day absence and enter Catch-Up Mode
Step 3: Verify overdue tasks are grouped by domain
Step 4: Verify one-tap actions: reschedule, backlog, drop
Step 5: Process all 15 tasks
Step 6: Verify the entire flow can be completed efficiently

description: Fresh Start Mode activates for 7+ day absence — bulk overdue sweep, project health check, simplified day plan
steps: Step 1: Set up data simulating 10 days of absence with 20 overdue tasks and 15 unprocessed inbox items
Step 2: Create 5 active projects with last_touched_at older than 10 days
Step 3: Navigate to the Cockpit
Step 4: Verify Fresh Start Mode activates (not Catch-Up Mode)
Step 5: Verify the tone is welcoming — 'Welcome back' style, not guilt-inducing
Step 6: Verify bulk overdue resolution: one-action sweep moves non-deadline tasks to project backlogs
Step 7: Verify hard-deadline tasks are preserved for individual triage
Step 8: Verify project health check: checkbox list showing each active project with Keep/Pause options
Step 9: Verify inbox deferral: option to defer inbox processing with a suggested processing time
Step 10: Complete the fresh start flow and verify a simplified day plan is created
Step 11: Verify no retroactive daily_plans were created for missed days

description: Fresh Start Mode: bulk sweep moves all non-deadline overdue tasks to project backlogs in one action
steps: Step 1: Create 20 overdue tasks — 5 with due dates (hard deadlines), 15 without
Step 2: Enter Fresh Start Mode
Step 3: Use the bulk sweep action
Step 4: Verify the 15 non-deadline tasks are returned to their project backlogs
Step 5: Verify the 5 deadline tasks remain flagged for individual triage

description: No retroactive daily plans: system only creates daily plans for today and forward, never for missed days
steps: Step 1: Simulate a 5-day absence
Step 2: Open the app and complete catch-up or fresh start
Step 3: Verify only one daily_plan was created (for today)
Step 4: Verify no daily_plan rows exist for the missed days

description: Full keyboard navigation: all primary screens, buttons, and interactive elements are accessible via Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Escape
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the app and press Tab
Step 2: Verify focus moves to the first sidebar navigation item with a visible focus indicator
Step 3: Press Tab repeatedly — verify focus moves through all sidebar items in order
Step 4: Press Enter on the Projects nav item — verify the Projects screen loads
Step 5: Press Tab — verify focus moves into the main content area (domain tabs, project cards)
Step 6: Press Enter on a project card — verify the project opens
Step 7: Press Tab through task items — verify each has a focus indicator
Step 8: Press Escape to close modals or return to previous view
Step 9: Navigate to Inbox and Tab to the capture field — type and press Enter to create an item
Step 10: Verify Shift+Tab moves focus backwards through the interface

description: Color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA minimum (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) across all screens
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Inbox screen and take a screenshot
Step 2: Verify text elements have sufficient contrast against their backgrounds
Step 3: Navigate to the Cockpit and verify contrast on the capacity bar labels
Step 4: Navigate to Projects and verify contrast on project cards and task text
Step 5: Verify domain color badges have readable text

description: Responsive sidebar: collapses to icons-only when browser window is narrower than 1024px
steps: Step 1: Open the app in a wide browser window (>1024px)
Step 2: Verify the sidebar shows full labels (Inbox, Cockpit, Projects, Review, Settings)
Step 3: Resize the window to under 1024px
Step 4: Verify the sidebar collapses to show only icons
Step 5: Verify navigation still works by clicking icons

description: Loading states: skeleton screens or spinners display while data is being fetched
steps: Step 1: Navigate to the Projects screen
Step 2: Verify a loading state (skeleton or spinner) appears briefly before content renders
Step 3: Navigate to the Cockpit
Step 4: Verify appropriate loading states during data fetch

description: Error states: display user-friendly error messages when API calls fail, with retry options
steps: Step 1: Simulate a backend API failure (e.g., stop the server briefly)
Step 2: Attempt an action in the UI (e.g., create a task)
Step 3: Verify a user-friendly error message appears (not a raw error or blank screen)
Step 4: Verify a retry option is available

description: Hover states and focus indicators: all buttons, links, cards, and interactive elements have visible hover and focus states
steps: Step 1: Hover over sidebar navigation items — verify hover state (background change, color shift)
Step 2: Hover over project cards — verify hover state
Step 3: Hover over task checkboxes — verify hover indicator
Step 4: Tab through interactive elements — verify focus ring/outline is visible

description: 'I have another device' option at first launch offers device pairing flow instead of fresh setup
steps: Step 1: Start the app with a fresh database
Step 2: Verify the setup wizard's first screen includes an 'I have another device' option
Step 3: Click the option
Step 4: Verify a device pairing flow initiates (6-digit code entry or display)

description: Settings: database size display shows current SQLite file size
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Data Management
Step 2: Verify the current database size is displayed (e.g., '2.4 MB')
Step 3: Add some data (create tasks, projects)
Step 4: Verify the size display updates

description: Settings: JSON data export — export all data as JSON file for backup
steps: Step 1: Navigate to Settings > Data Management
Step 2: Click 'Export Data'
Step 3: Verify a JSON file is downloaded or saved
Step 4: Open the JSON file and verify it contains domains, projects, tasks, and other entity data

description: Settings: soft-delete purge — purge rows with deleted_at older than 90 days
steps: Step 1: Create and soft-delete some tasks, setting deleted_at to 100 days ago
Step 2: Navigate to Settings > Data Management
Step 3: Run the purge operation
Step 4: Verify the soft-deleted rows older than 90 days have been hard-deleted
Step 5: Verify recently soft-deleted rows (under 90 days) remain untouched
